title: 1375 · Catalan Atlas
about: The realms and regions of the Catalan Atlas (Cresques Abraham, Majorca, conventionally 1375; BnF Espagnol 30), lettered in the atlas's own spelling (name) or in a modern English reading (reading). Each is a point with a zoom band [from, to): lettered while from <= zoom < to, and the Regions slider still caps it. Earlier entries win where two names meet. legend is the atlas's own legend in translation, where it has one; note is ours; sheet is the BnF sheet (5 to 12) where the name or its ruler is drawn. See docs/period-names/README.md.

sources.name: The Cresques Project, translations of the legends, panels III to VI
BnF Gallica, Atlas de cartes marines dit Atlas catalan
Wikimedia Commons, Catalan Atlas BNF, sheets 5 to 12 (public domain)

names.name: Sarra
names.legend: Here resides the emperor of this northern region, whose empire starts in the province of Bulgaria and ends in the city of Organcio. The sovereign is named Jambech, Lord of Sarra.
names.note: Jambech is Jani Beg, khan of the Golden Horde to 1357; Sarra is Sarai on the Volga.

names.name: Catayo
names.legend: The most powerful prince of the Tartars is named Holubeim, that means Great Khan. Here ends Catay.
names.note: Holubeim is Kublai Khan; the Yuan fell to the Ming in 1368.

names.name: Medeja
names.legend: Here reigns the King Chabech, lord of the empire of Medeja. He resides at Emalech.
names.note: Chabech is Kebek, khan of the Chagatai to 1326; Emalech is Almaliq.

names.name: Tauris
names.note: Lettered Rey del Tauris, the king of Tabriz, crowned and seated over the cities of Persia. The Il-Khanate had broken up by 1335; in 1375 Tabriz was the Jalayirids'.

names.name: Melly
names.legend: This black lord is called Musse Melly and is the sovereign of the land of the blacks of Gineva. This king is the richest and noblest lord of all this land, for the abundance of gold that is gathered in his land.
names.note: Musse Melly is Mansa Musa; Ciutat de Melly, the city of Mali, is drawn beside him.

names.name: Delli
names.legend: Here resides a great sultan, powerful and very rich. The sultan has seven hundred elephants and one hundred thousand horsemen under his command.

names.name: Babillonia
names.legend: This sultan of Babylon is great and powerful amongst those of this region.
names.note: Babylon of Egypt: Fustat, by Cairo.

names.name: Arabia Sebba
names.legend: The province that had queen Sebba; now it belongs to the Arab Saracens.

names.name: Organa
names.legend: Here rules the King of Organa, a Saracen that constantly battles with the Saracens of the coast and with other Arabs.

names.name: Nubia
names.legend: The king of Nubia is always at war with the Christians of Nubia, who are under the dominion of the emperor of Ethiopia and the land of Prester John.

names.name: Tarsia
names.legend: This province is called Tarsia, and it is from which the three very wise kings departed.

names.name: Gog e Magog
names.legend: The great lord prince of Gog and Magog.

names.name: Turquia
names.legend: Asia Minor, also called Turkey, where there are many cities and castles.

names.name: França
names.note: No realm is lettered: its towns fly the lilies. The atlas was in the French royal library by 1380.

names.name: Panonia
names.note: Its city of Albargala, Székesfehérvár, flies the Angevin kings' blue, gold and red.

names.name: Caldea
names.legend: Here there was the Great Babylonia, where Nabuconodosor resided, and that is called Baldaca today.

names.name: Persia
names.legend: Across from the mouth of the river of Baldach lie the sea of the Indies and of Persia.

names.name: Indies
names.legend: This city is named Hormes and is the beginning of the Indies.

names.name: Aragó
names.note: No realm is lettered: the Crown's red and gold pales fly over its towns. The atlas was made in Majorca, under the Crown.

names.name: Nuruega
names.legend: This region of Norway is very rugged, very cold, mountainous, wild and covered with forests.

names.name: Granada
names.note: Granada's flag is lettered in Arabic and marked with a cross: perhaps the Nasrids' vassalage to Castile.

names.name: Sicilia
names.note: The island flies the kingdom's flag: four pales and two eagles.

names.name: Constantinoble
names.note: No realm is lettered: the city and its flag stand for what was left of the empire.

names.name: Colombo
names.legend: Here reigns the king of Colombo, a Christian. Province of Colombo.
names.note: Colombo is Kollam, on the Malabar coast.
